evidence: The paper does not report or interpret impurity importance from the Random Forests. Instead, it uses Random Forest predictions as transformed covariates in a second-stage model: "This process can therefore be seen as creating non-linear transformations of the raw covariates that are hopefully better correlated with malaria incidence." Table 5 reports only RMSE (model-level predictive error) and regression coefficients for the predictions, not feature-level importances within the Random Forests. The paper validates using held-out out-of-sample prediction performance across random and spatial cross-validation folds.
